references.text: Abraham raises his hand toward heaven and swears by the Lord, the Most High God, as an expression of a solemn oath.
God raises His hand as a sign of His oath to give the land to the children of Israel.
The Lord swears by Himself with the phrase 'as surely as I live', expressing God's eternal existence.
God uses the oath 'as surely as I live' to confirm His judgment and actions.
The Lord raises His hand and swears to the descendants of Israel, referring to God's solemn oath.
The man raises his right and left hands toward heaven and swears by Him who lives forever.
The angel raises his hand toward heaven and swears by Him who lives for all eternity, a direct parallel to God's oath.
God swears by Himself because there is no one greater to swear by, expressing God's eternal and unchangeable nature.
